summary.headline: Omnitech FY26 consolidated revenue rose 49.1% to INR 511.3 crore and PAT rose 80.9% to INR 79.3 crore, with order book at about INR 3,000 crore as of May 25, 2026.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 49.1% to INR 511.3 crore, EBITDA rose 45.4% to INR 171.1 crore, and PAT margin widened to 15.5% from 12.8%. Q4 revenue grew 38.5% to INR 148.7 crore, with PAT up 43.4% to INR 29.3 crore at a 19.7% margin, though management acknowledged a sharp gross margin compression in Q4. Working capital rose to INR 294 crore on higher inventory (MOQ-driven) and receivable days of 153, while payable days improved to 80 from 64. The order book was stated at around INR 3,000 crore, led by a multi-year Weatherford order of more than INR 900 crore and a second oilfield-services order of about INR 1,000 crore, both expected to ramp from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +92% YoY (stated as nearly doubled up to 92%)
from 16.1% / 21.6%; diluted by larger IPO-driven equity base (INR 203 crore to INR 679 crore)
expected to be realised in FY27

segments.name: Energy (incl. oil and gas)
segments.commentary: 53% of FY26 revenue and 74% of the order book. Weatherford multi-year order is more than INR 900 crore over five years, with management indicating a ramp of roughly 70% in year one.

segments.name: Motion control and automation
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue and 14% of the order book. Management says over 90% of this segment's revenue comes from repeat customers with short order cycles of three to four months.

segments.name: Industrial equipment
segments.commentary: About 16% of FY26 revenue and about 12% of the order book.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Plants at Metoda and Chhapara certified to AS9100; NADCAP process initiated for surface treatment, NDT and welding. Four FA development orders received; no revenue quantified for FY27-28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided in line with the historical 30-35% range (CFO: 'similar growth in this year also'); management also cited a planning figure of roughly +/-5% around about 30%.

EBITDA margin guided at about 30-35% on an average basis, per management; CFO said margin will be 'similar as per the historical'. Management attributed Q4 margin compression to costs incurred in advance of FY27 growth (people, key talent, first-article development).

Three FY27 initiatives: commissioning a new facility in Hyderabad (leased, small, closer to defence customers), expanding a proposed new facility at Chhapara, and solar roofing at existing Chhapara plant.

Management said existing capacity covers FY27 and early FY28 (Q1-Q2); new capacity of about 2.6 million machine hours (later referred to as 1.5 million additional hours) to be ramping from after Q1 FY27 and contributing from FY28-29.
Management described Q4 margin compression as a result of growth-linked costs and said it expects better margins in future quarters, without giving a specific number.
capex_capacity: Annualised capacity of 26 lakh hours, with precision capability up to 5 microns; management says existing plant can support about 750-800 (units not specified) and additional 1.5 million machining hours planned for FY29 onwards.

Two facilities being built at Chhapara using IPO proceeds; new facility to start ramping after Q1 FY27. Management referenced about 2.6 million hours with new capacity, rising to more than 4 million machine hours.
Hyderabad facility is a leased property, described as small units close to defence customers; commissioning in FY27.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad for growth beyond FY28-29.
Investment in 17,000 PSI over-pressure testing for assembly work on one multi-year order.
demand_pricing: Order book grew from INR 57 crore (FY23) to INR 83 crore (FY24) and INR 283 crore (FY25) to about INR 3,000 crore as of May 25, 2026. Geography mix: North America about 64%, Asia 34%, India 1.5%, Europe/UK 0.5%.
FY26 revenue mix by geography: North America 53%, India 24%, Asia 19%, Europe/UK about 4%. Around 75% of revenue from outside India; 256+ customers across 24 countries.
Pricing pass-through: management said raw material pass-through is standard practice; most business is ex-works, so customers bear logistics and raw-material risk. No quantified lag disclosed.
Management said there was no major tariff impact on US sales. Seasonality was described as only +/-5-10% and no material quarter-on-quarter seasonality.
Management stated the addressable oil and gas opportunity is large but declined to quantify it; it noted SLB, Weatherford, Halliburton, NOV, TechnipFMC as potential customers.

qa_highlights.question: How tentative is the Weatherford master purchase agreement (INR 184 crore per year schedule), and what is the ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Weatherford is an existing customer and orders follow its yearly and quarterly requirements under long-term agreements. Roughly INR 900 crore over five years, with about 70% in year one and rising in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the second large order (about INR 1,000 crore) an MPA, and when does revenue begin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is similar in nature, with revenue starting in FY27 for some product lines and early FY28 for others. Management did not name the customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 gross margin compression a one-time item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth-linked costs incurred in late Q3 and Q4 are being absorbed ahead of FY27 growth, and that this should yield results in FY27. The CFO guided to margins in line with historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is embedded in the Weatherford contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share the Weatherford margin, but said the company's average EBITDA target across the customer base is about 1-2% above or below the stated average.

qa_highlights.question: How much more can the existing capacity deliver before new capacity comes online?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing capacity covers FY27 and early FY28 (Q1-Q2) with a few bottleneck machines to be added. Beyond that, the new Chhapara capacity is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace revenue outlook for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number due to long FA approval cycles, but said some aerospace revenue was booked in FY26 and it expects good growth in FY27.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivable days of 153 and inventory build from MOQ commitments; management targets normalisation by fiscal year-end through inventory rationalisation and receivable collection.
Margin: Q4 gross margin fell sharply (about 450 bps versus the prior two quarters per an analyst); whether margins recover to historical levels in FY27 remains to be seen.

Weatherford and the second large order are described as contingent on customer scheduling, and the Weatherford schedule was not confirmed. Some Middle East exposure was acknowledged, with minor shipment delays.
Talent and execution: scaling Rajkot operations and ramping new capacity from Q1 FY27; Hyderabad facility commissioning timing.
Aerospace and defence revenue contribution remains unquantified; management says FA approvals take long lead times.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order book, but evasive on quantification: management declined to size the oil and gas addressable market, the Weatherford margin, and aerospace revenue. Margin questions were answered with reassurance and no hard numbers beyond a 30-35% range.
